trust_decision.summary: The RBAC metastore trusts a 64-bit-truncated MD5 of the grantee key as a unique identifier that binds a role/object/collection grant to its privilege-record subtree (grantee-id/<id>/<privilege>); every read, delete and rename of grants keys off that id, so two distinct grantees can share one id and each other's privileges/records.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'grantee-id uses truncated MD5'; the first code a reader lands on is where the grantee id is minted for a grant, `idStr = crypto.MD5(k)`, then written under GranteeIDPrefix at kv_catalog.go:1374. The 64-bit truncation itself sits one package away in pkg/util/crypto.

gRPC SelectGrant (internal/rootcoord/root_coord.go:2713) -> Catalog.ListGrant; also Catalog.BackupRBAC (kv_catalog.go:1773) and the revoke bookkeeping in internal/rootcoord/rbac_task.go:86

O3_reason_to_dismiss: crypto.MD5 is a generic shared util whose 16-char contract is asserted by its own test and by already-persisted metadata, so a solver can argue the truncation itself is out of RBAC scope and only the two minting call sites need the new full-length hash; the pre-existing 16-char ids then look like legacy data that 'is not part of this bug'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Grants written before the fix carry 16-char ids and may live under the legacy no-db grantee key (role/object/collectionName) instead of the db-qualified key; a fix that just recomputes ids or prefix-deletes old grantee-id subtrees makes live grants unreadable and silently drops other roles' privilege records. A stored id can also be 16 chars without being the MD5 of its key (the fix's own 'unreferenced computed legacy id' case), so length alone must not trigger migration/collision handling.

O6_input_shapes: legacy no-db grantee key (role/object/collectionName) vs db-qualified key (role/object/db.collection)
wildcard-db key (role/object/*.collectionName) consulted as a ListGrant fallback
16-char stored id (legacy, kv_catalog.go:1366) vs 32-char full-length id
a 16-char stored id that is not the MD5 of its grantee key (unreferenced computed legacy id)
one 16-char id referenced by two different grantee keys (shared/colliding id), in both the read and delete paths
collection rename: old name -> new name, with child grantee-id entries moved and the old parent removed
backup/restore: grants serialized in RBACMeta without any id, re-minted on restore
single-role query vs tenant-wide prefix scan of all grantees

O8b_injection_room.sibling: RestoreRBAC writing GranteePrefix/GranteeIDPrefix entries directly from the backup blob instead of re-minting through AlterGrant
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the backup already carries role/object/objectName per grant, so a bulk write looks cheaper and would bypass the id derivation and the shared-id check entirely

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a third prefix-deletion path (e.g. DropDatabase or DropPartition grant cleanup) reusing the DeleteGrantByCollectionName loop
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: DeleteGrantByCollectionName and DeleteGrant already duplicate the same prefix-remove pattern, so a maintainer adding another drop path would copy it, including the unguarded prefix removal

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a background grantee-id GC that walks the GranteeIDPrefix and deletes all 16-char (legacy) ids
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the package already has a prefix-walking background sweeper that deletes keys by value shape; a 'clean up legacy ids' migration job written the same way would delete subtrees shared by two roles

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second short-id helper copied from MD5 for another RBAC object (privilege group, user-role key)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the truncated MD5 helper is exported from a shared package and already used as a general key-hashing idiom, so copying it for a neighbouring id is the path of least resistance

O9_family: identifier derivation with a 64-bit-truncated MD5 (CWE-327): grantee-id collision leading to cross-role privilege binding, plus the legacy-id migration/cleanup semantics around that identifier

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace crypto.MD5 with the full-length hash at the two minting sites (kv_catalog.go:1366 and 1597) and stop there: new grants get 32-char ids, but existing 16-char ids are neither migrated nor read, and the delete/rename paths still prefix-delete subtrees that a second grantee shares.

out_of_scope_notes: AlterGrant builds its grantee key without funcutil.HandleTenantForEtcdPrefix (kv_catalog.go:1338) while ListGrant and DeleteGrant do add the tenant prefix (kv_catalog.go:1475, kv_catalog.go:1641) - a tenancy inconsistency next to this sink, not covered by this advisory and not pursued.
